artists.biography: Pop Will Eat Itself (also known as PWEI or The Poppies) are an English alternative rock band, originally formed in Stourbridge in 1986, with members from Birmingham, Coventry and the Black Country. Initially known as a Grebo act, their style changed to incorporate sample driven indie and industrial rock. Their highest charting single was 1993's "Get The Girl! Kill The Baddies!". After initially disbanding in 1996, and having a brief reformation in 2005, they issued their first release in over five years in 2010.

perplexity.description:
Wise Up Suckers is a compilation album by the English alternative band Pop Will Eat Itself, originally released in 1996. The album gathers a selection of 17 tracks that showcase the band’s fusion of electronic and rock elements, reflecting their pioneering blend of hip-hop, dance, and rock styles that defined much of their late 1980s and early 1990s output. This compilation serves as a retrospective overview rather than a studio album, capturing the band’s evolution and their signature sample-heavy, guitar-driven sound.

In the context of Pop Will Eat Itself’s discography, Wise Up Suckers follows their active period culminating in the mid-1990s, shortly before their initial disbandment in 1996. It highlights the band’s role in the alternative and electronic rock scenes, particularly their innovative approach to integrating drum machines, samples, and rap-style vocals with rock instrumentation. While not a commercial studio release, the compilation provides a curated experience of their influential work, appealing to both longtime fans and newcomers interested in their genre-crossing style.

Critically, Pop Will Eat Itself has been recognized for their energetic and eclectic sound, with tracks like “Wise Up! Sucker” (from their 1989 album This Is the Day...This Is the Hour...This Is This!) exemplifying their dark, drum-heavy, and sample-rich style. Although Wise Up Suckers itself is a compilation and thus not subject to traditional album reviews, it consolidates the band’s legacy during a period when they were regarded as innovators in alternative electronic rock. The album was released on the Music On Vinyl label in a reissue format, but its original 1996 release marks its place as a key retrospective in the band’s catalog.
